Yes. The subtext enriches the setting rather than feeling forced. The stranger’s scrutiny of the ferry’s equipment and his timing of the crossing suggest an official assessment—and a possible threat to Ilse’s livelihood—without stating his purpose. Her refusal to return his wave and her unanswered call from Jonas imply unease beneath her outward composure.

These tensions emerge naturally from the ferry’s everyday routines. The fog also echoes Ilse’s uncertain future without losing its practical role in the river setting.
